name: supervised-unsupervised-rl-feedback-loop
explain: Demonstrates fundamental feedback mechanisms across Supervised (ground-truth target loss minimization), Unsupervised (geometric inertia reduction without outcome labels), and Reinforcement Learning (scalar evaluative reward in contextual bandits).
steps: Fit supervised regressor against ground-truth targets || Cluster transactions with 1D K-Means and prove clusters do not represent policy labels || Optimize contextual bandit arm selection under epsilon-greedy exploration.
expect: All supervised, unsupervised, and RL feedback loop assertions verified successfully.
limit: Simulates 1D and scalar feedback mechanisms; does not train deep RL actor-critic policies.

name: temporal-as-of-feature-leakage-guard
explain: Demonstrates temporal data leakage when warehouse columns populated post-decision are extracted as features, and implements an as-of point-in-time feature extraction guard.
steps: Extract leaky features populated at ticket resolution to show trivial 100% target proxy || Enforce point-in-time as-of timestamp guard at ticket creation time || Verify temporal causality invariant rejecting future evaluation timestamps.
expect: All temporal as-of feature leakage guard assertions verified successfully.
limit: Simulates temporal feature extraction logic; does not connect to a distributed feature store backend.

name: cost-sensitive-classification-threshold-optimizer
explain: Demonstrates the separation between model probabilities and operational decision thresholds, optimizing thresholds under asymmetric business error costs (e.g. false negative fraud cost versus false positive verification cost).
steps: Implement numerically stable sigmoid and binary cross-entropy log loss || Define asymmetric business cost matrix ( FP vs  FN) || Sweep decision thresholds to prove optimal operational threshold beats default 0.5 by >60% cost reduction.
expect: All cost-sensitive classification threshold optimizer assertions verified successfully.
limit: Optimizes scalar decision threshold on static validation probabilities; does not perform online bandit threshold tuning.

name: ensemble-bias-variance-decomposition
explain: Demonstrates the bias-variance trade-off across Decision Trees, Random Forest Bagging (variance reduction via bootstrap aggregation), and Gradient Boosting (bias reduction via sequential residual fitting).
steps: Fit single decision stump demonstrating high bias on non-linear target || Fit gradient boosted stumps demonstrating sequential bias reduction || Evaluate prediction variance across resampled training sets to prove bagging variance reduction.
expect: All ensemble bias-variance decomposition assertions verified successfully.
limit: Implements 1D decision stumps; does not evaluate multi-feature tree splits or GPU histogram boosting.

name: unsupervised-cluster-boundary-validation
explain: Demonstrates scale sensitivity in distance-based clustering where unscaled large-magnitude features monopolize Euclidean boundaries, and proves why unsupervised clusters cannot serve as authoritative business policy labels.
steps: Execute K-Means on unscaled customer data, proving transaction dollars completely dominate age || Apply z-score standardization to incorporate both age and transaction dimensions into Euclidean distance || Assert cluster assignments cannot replace supervised policy calibration.
expect: All unsupervised cluster boundary validation assertions verified successfully.
limit: Evaluates 2D K-Means clustering; does not train deep representation autoencoders.

name: early-stopping-patience-regularization-guard
explain: Demonstrates early stopping on validation loss trajectories with patience windows, restores optimal model checkpoint weights, and guards against test-set contamination.
steps: Simulate training trajectory where training loss falls while validation loss begins diverging || Execute early stopping manager with patience 3 halting at optimal validation checkpoint || Verify test set evaluation remains uncompromised and untouched during stopping decisions.
expect: All early stopping patience regularization guard assertions verified successfully.
limit: Simulates scalar loss trajectories; does not execute multi-epoch PyTorch training loops.

name: imbalanced-precision-recall-curve-evaluator
explain: Demonstrates the accuracy paradox on imbalanced datasets where a dummy majority-class model achieves 80% accuracy with 0.0 recall, and evaluates full Precision-Recall curves across decision thresholds.
steps: Evaluate 4-negative 1-positive case proving dummy classifier accuracy paradox || Compute full confusion matrices across decision thresholds on 1,000 imbalanced samples || Prove monotonic trade-off between precision and recall on positive class.
expect: All imbalanced precision-recall curve evaluator assertions verified successfully.
limit: Evaluates offline binary classification metrics; does not simulate streaming drift.

name: probability-calibration-brier-reliability-diagram
explain: Demonstrates the decoupling between discrimination (ROC-AUC ranking) and probability calibration, evaluating Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score.
steps: Construct two models with identical perfect ROC-AUC = 1.0 || Compute Brier score proving uncalibrated model incurs severe probability penalty || Calculate Expected Calibration Error across 5 confidence bins proving ECE drops from >0.40 to <0.05 on calibrated probabilities.
expect: All probability calibration Brier reliability diagram assertions verified successfully.
limit: Calculates binned calibration statistics; does not fit non-parametric isotonic regression calibrators.

name: distribution-shift-drift-detector
explain: Demonstrates the taxonomy and detection of distribution shifts: Covariate Shift P(X) via Population Stability Index (PSI), Target Shift P(Y), and Concept Drift P(Y|X) via delayed label error tracking.
steps: Compute Population Stability Index on baseline versus current feature distributions || Detect covariate shift when PSI exceeds 0.20 threshold || Distinguish concept drift when input distributions remain stable but delayed ground-truth error rates spike.
expect: All distribution shift drift detector assertions verified successfully.
limit: Evaluates 1D feature drift and scalar error rates; does not execute high-dimensional multivariate embedding drift.
